server/lib/ai/output-classification.ts#C.reason: States that model-assisted text of this class must be reviewed by a person before a client reads it. Its reader is review, not code, and nothing should branch on it - because on the path where it applies the review is STRUCTURAL rather than flag-driven. server/api/ai.ts writes nothing but the review row: the assist routes RETURN rewritten text and a person puts it into the report, and the route refuses to hand the UI a suggestion with no aiCallId precisely so that text an inspector cannot review is text they cannot accept. The field was also on all twelve postures including the eight that refuse the call; it now sits only on the four that may produce output. No rule this deployment is held to requires a publish-time review gate. The requirement that exists is narrower: machine translation must not be delivered as AUTHORITATIVE LEGAL TEXT without human legal review, and descriptive findings and ordinary narrative may be machine translated. The two classes that would have needed a reviewer, legal_text and repair_pricing, are prohibited on both sources instead - the requirement is met by refusal, not by review.
